risks: Low: the adaptations change how the programme is offered, not its content. Risks are intrusion when contacting people who have left and loss of group connection in video sessions.
consent: People are told at referral that the clinic is evaluating changes to the programme; consent is asked for follow-up contact after leaving and for conversations, which are optional and do not affect care.
data: Attendance and questionnaires stay in the clinic record; the evaluation file holds study codes only and is kept on the hospital drive for five years.
equity: PROGRESS-Plus: employment, reliance on public transport and language spoken at home are the suspected barriers. Interpreters are offered for the orientation call and conversations, video help is offered before the first hybrid session, and completion is reported by each barrier so the adaptations are judged by whom they reach.
effectiveness: Success is higher completion and reach without loss of pain interference benefit or group connection.
efficiency: The orientation call costs about 20 minutes per starter; follow-up of leavers about two hours a week.
costs: Within existing staff time except the evening group, which depends on approval.
grants: None needed; a positive result could support a regional application to spread the adaptations.
partnerships: Clinic manager, the physiotherapist and psychologist, two former participants (one who left early), and the hospital interpreter service.
rebPath: The clinic will ask the research ethics board whether the evaluation is quality improvement or research needing full review; the decision is unknown, and no follow-up contact of leavers starts until it is made. Principles follow the TCPS 2 when the board applies it and ICH-GCP otherwise.
limitations: Single clinic, sequential adaptations that overlap in time, and likely low response from people who leave.
summary: Low-risk evaluation with consent for follow-up contact, equity reporting by barrier, and an ethics determination still unknown.
